_note: Candidate-specific registration wording for c3_registration.py (--frozen-from, --claim-wording, --branch-caps), drafted 2026-10-19 before the candidate is fixed (§0.1). Branch caps read from each harness's code at k = 5. The registration review checks them against the frozen file. E002.frozen_from: runs/c2-confirm2/frozen.py (sha e772bd6e...) = E002b, promoted 2026-10-16 as the dev incumbent: 4 Luna samples, then a Sol judge picks among the distinct public-green files (one green: submitted as is; none: a Luna repair). It passed C2-LOOK1. It was superseded as the dev incumbent on 2026-10-20 by E007 (Sol-directed repair; fresh dev confirmation +17.1 pp all-pass vs E002). E007 is not the candidate because its one permitted look (C2-LOOK2, 10-21) was invalid (one hidden-test-name hit), so under plan §0.1 the candidate is E002.
E002.claim_wording: At an equal invocation cap of 5 model calls per task, a two-model harness (at most 5 calls per task: 4 Luna samples, then either 1 Sol judge call at medium effort or 1 Luna repair) produces working software (every hidden test passes) more often than Luna alone in a plain repair loop (D, at most 5 Luna calls) and in best-of-5 with public-test selection (B). Not cost- or token-matched: Sol is a stronger model from the same vendor, X used about 4.6x D's tokens on dev, and no cost-matched control (e.g. D plus one Sol call) is run. Calls and tokens by lane are reported beside the claim.
E002.branch_caps: judge (>= 2 distinct public-green files): 4 Luna + 1 Sol; one-green: 4 Luna; no-green-repair: 4 Luna + 1 Luna. Never more than 5 calls, at most 1 Sol.
disclosures: Hidden-name exposure: the IntegrityReview rule counts any hidden-test name found as an identifier in any prompt, including model-written code that a later prompt carries (X's judge prompts carry Luna's files; D's repair prompts carry its previous attempt; B's prompts carry none). The observed base rate is about 1 coincidental hit per 2-3k such prompts (0 in 12,356 cycle-2 dev prompts, 0 in look 1 and in the confirmation-3 audits, and 1 in look 2, where a Luna draft named something exactly like a hidden test). With about 340 such prompts over two replicates, that is a rough 10-15% chance of an IntegrityReview with no leak. Confirmation-3's naming conventions may differ from the suites behind that rate. The rule is not narrowed (plan §0.10).

The frozen candidate is not the strongest harness found on dev: the dev incumbent E007 beat E002 there (+7.1 and +17.1 pp all-pass over two replicates), but its only permitted dev-holdout look was invalid. E007's advantage on this confirmation distribution is unmeasured; this test says nothing about E007.
